Maya: Heads-up 10k bring-up for VectorSherpa. FP32 recall@10 on short_seq_holdout = 0.750, PTQ6 (per-tensor) = 0.682 (delta -0.068). Quick repro below.
Jun: short_seq_holdout = queries <=6 tokens?
Maya: yep <=6. Commands I ran:
```bash
./eval_embeddings --model=vector_sherpa:fp32 --dataset=short_seq_holdout --metric=recall@10
./eval_embeddings --model=vector_sherpa:ptq6 --dataset=short_seq_holdout --metric=recall@10
```
Sample output:
```
fp32 recall@10: 0.750
ptq6 recall@10: 0.682
delta: -0.068 (~9.1%)
```
Rafael: two quick suspects: per-tensor quant scale bias (directional shift), or whitening/PCA applied differently pre/post-quant. Did you keep L2 norm and PCA identical?
Maya: preprocessing pipeline identical. I emulated per-channel quant on CPU for the linear layers and saw partial recovery -> recall@10 = 0.719.
Priya: thats promising. Next try: 4k asymmetric calibration samples + per-channel on projection matrix only, and a small 512-sample bias-correction on the final projection. Short queries are sensitive to small angular perturbations.
Jun: also capture recall@100 and MAP. If higher-k recovers, product can accept ptq for tail traffic.
Rafael: add a histogram of top-20 cosine sims and principal-angle between top-5 PCA components pre/post quant so we can detect rotation drift. If dists compress to narrow range after quant, knn breaks.
Maya: queued runs: (1) ptq6 per-channel with 4k calib asymmetric, (2) bias-corr 512 on proj, (3) disable range-fold on final linear, (4) produce recall@10/@100/MAP + hist + PCA-angle. ETA ~1.5h on staging.
ci-bot: test-run vector-sherpa ptq6-perchannel started (run id: rs-2026-09-07-02).
Maya: for release notes mark vector_sherpa/ptq6 as "requires per-channel calibration" and DO NOT enable as default in canary until short-query parity is validated. Ping @Rafael @Priya for follow-ups when runs complete.
